solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.meaning: a tiny division of time, one sixtieth of a minute
to back a motion or a candidate is to ... it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as the sixty-second unit, but it is the adjective 'tiny' (my-NOOT); 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a very small slice of time, and to second a proposal is to back it, so both senses fit.

definitions.meaning: the long key at the bottom of a computer keyboard is the ... bar
room in the sense of free area or capacity

explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard's long key is the space bar, and room to move is open area, the same word in both senses.

indicators.note: the second word becomes what the first one contains, sitting inside it as its contents

parts.note: a medicine is a cure
appropriate means apt

explanation.surface: Advice to take a drug that suits the patient's condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... contents' signals one word holding another; 'Take' is a verb, as in seizing a prisoner or a city, not the medicine-taking the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize someone or something by force is to take it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Times supplier has fresh herb with neat edges

parts.note: fresh means new
sage is a herb

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from neat

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who stocks The Times also sells fresh herbs, neatly trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' with its capital looks like the hour, but it is the newspaper; a newsagent is a British corner shop selling papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is the shop that sells newspapers such as The Times.

clue.text: Gag held by extremely enormous arms

indicators.note: the first piece is held inside the letters supplied by the next words
the extreme ends of the word enormous, its first and last letters

parts.note: a gag is a joke, a quip

explanation.surface: A joke told by someone with huge arms, or a gag clamped in giant arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' is the verb, to give weapons or equipment to.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm someone is to supply them with weapons, which is to fit them out.

definitions.meaning: a monarch's spouse, a royal wife
the British group of Freddie Mercury

explanation.definitionFit: A king's wife is his royal partner, and the rock group fronted by Freddie Mercury bore the same title.

clue.text: I retain misplaced tendency to stay put

indicators.note: letters put out of their places are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps things in the wrong place is reluctant to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges the seven letters of I RETAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a body at rest stays at rest unless pushed, and in everyday speech it is sluggishness.

clue.text: Miss end of State capital's ceremony

indicators.note: drop the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Sacramento is the state capital of California

explanation.surface: Someone skips the closing part of a formal event in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss end of' removes the final O from SACRAMENTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament such as baptism is a solemn religious rite.

parts.note: an animal's padded foot is a paw
an animal paws at something when it scratches it

explanation.surface: A cat's paw scratches some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' looks like a verb, but it is the soft foot of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawpaws are papayas, tropical fruit.

parts.note: the prefix de- means taking away, as in defrost
a fence is a barrier

explanation.surface: Taking away a fence leaves a property unguarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a made-up verb, DE-FENCE means 'remove barrier', while the surface suggests the barrier is the protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence is a means of guarding against attack.

clue.text: Chinese gooseberry causes a lot of Turkish wi-fi disruption

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown out of order and rearranged
most but not all of the word, here losing its last two letters

parts.note: the word as written, trimmed

explanation.surface: Turkish internet suffers outages, blamed on an exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims TURKISH to TURKI; 'disruption' rearranges TURKI plus WIFI.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi fruit was once marketed as the Chinese gooseberry, its older name.

indicators.note: one letter is swapped for another, here altering the musical volume marking

parts.note: a person's character is their reputation

explanation.surface: A rebuttal that alters how loud a character speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: In music P (piano) means soft and F (forte) loud; changing the loudness swaps P for F in REPUTATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A refutation is an argument that disproves a claim, a rebuttal.

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from tonic

parts.note: rap is slang for talk or chat

explanation.surface: A gin and tonic starts a conversation at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the drink but a snare, as in a gin trap; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals, a kind of trap.

definitions.meaning: a work of art or music, such as a piano composition
a portion or fragment of something
a clock or watch, a timepiece, is a kind of instrument for time

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'part-time' look like one word, but it is two definitions; the third is timepiece, of which 'time, maybe' is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition is a piece, a fragment is a piece, and a watch is a timepiece, so all three fit.

clue.text: In favour of proposal for raising level

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Supporting a proposal to raise the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion lifts someone to a higher rank.

indicators.note: the word Bond is left out and the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: James Bond abandoned, alone and covered in blood.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B, O, N, D out of BLOODSTAINED: 'left' removes them and 'terribly' rearranges what is left, LOSTAIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserted place is cut off and alone, remote from others.

clue.text: Black vote halved after very large swing

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
Cilla Black, the British singer and TV presenter

indicators.note: only the last half of the word vote is kept

explanation.surface: A large shift in the black vote, reduced by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the singer and the half-vote behind the size label. Cilla Black was a British pop singer and presenter of TV's Blind Date; OS (outsize) marks very large clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to move back and forth, as a pendulum does.

clue.text: Tablet maybe stuck in rising star

indicators.note: the word for stuck goes inside the word for rising star

parts.note: an up-and-comer, a comer, is someone on the rise
stuck it there means put it there

explanation.surface: A pill caught inside a celebrity on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' looks like a pill, but it is the handheld device, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is one kind of portable electronic machine.

clue.text: Issue puzzle that is hard to teach

definitions.meaning: a matter of difficulty or concern
a question to be worked out, as in a chess or maths exercise
used as an adjective, as in a difficult child at school

explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link; the third sense is the adjective, as in a 'problem child'.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficulty, a teaser to solve, and an adjective for an unruly pupil all share the word.

parts.note: the leader of cheer is its first letter, C
warm gives heat

explanation.surface: A cheerleader wears a warm fleece jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheerleader' is not a pom-pom waver but the leading letter of 'cheer'; 'fleece' is the verb, to swindle, and 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them.

indicators.note: the letters are designed afresh into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The laciest lingerie design is elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges LACIEST; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material springs back after being pulled.

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
the plural gives a second go

explanation.surface: Someone takes turns at the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; go-go dancing is lively dancing in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-go describes energetic disco dancing, as by go-go dancers.

clue.text: Excellence of fish I like with head off

parts.note: brill is a flatfish

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to like something is to fancy it

explanation.surface: Admiring the quality of a fish that has had its head removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head off' takes F from FANCY, leaving ANCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliancy is outstanding skill or brightness, chess's term for a dazzling game.

indicators.note: letters running wild are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Begin a wild fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges BEGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spell of excess, a fling of indulgence.

clue.text: Mind game involves checking on board

definitions.text: Mind game involves checking on board

parts.words: Mind game involves checking on board
parts.note: a cerebral contest played on a board where one puts the opponent's king in check

explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game of strategy in which a king is put in check.

indicators.note: the first word coats or surrounds the second

parts.note: a wing is part of a bird
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A poorly prepared coating on a portion of chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' signals one word wrapped round another; 'prepared' means ready and keen, not cooked as the bird surface implies.
explanation.definitionFit: Being willing means being ready and happy to do something.

indicators.note: letters set out weirdly are rearranged into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Advice to move so as to act less strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weirdly' rearranges ACT LESS; 'to' is a link. In chess, a king castles.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is a chess move with king and rook; the blogger thinks the clue wanted 'Moves'.

definitions.meaning: more numb, as a frozen finger
a written symbol such as a digit

explanation.definitionFit: Numb-er means having less feeling, and a numeral is a character, so the one spelling fits both.

indicators.note: the letters go wrong and come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone traces wrong answers on a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges TRACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers in the verb sense means responds.
